title: Postproduction Processing of Electrospun Fibres for Tissue Engineering
protocol: Coat the rotating mandrel collector with aluminium foil, with the polished/shiny side facing outwards.
Prepare polymer solutions; make PLA, PCL and PHBV as a 10 wt% solution in DCM.
Make PLGA as a 20 wt% solution in DCM.
Place 4 syringes of 5 ml volume on a syringe pump.
Load syringes to contain 5 ml of the polymer each, giving 20 ml in total.
Use a flow rate of 40 μL/min per syringe for PLA, PCL and PHBV.
Use a flow rate of 30 μL/min per syringe for PLGA.
Maintain a working distance of 17 cm from needle tip to mandrel for PLA, PCL and PLGA.
Maintain a working distance of 10 cm from needle tip to mandrel for PHBV.
Charge the syringe needles to +17000 V (73030 P, Genvolt, Shropshire, UK).
Electrospin from the appropriate distance onto the aluminium foil coated mandrel.
Rotate the mandrel at 200 rpm for random fibres.
Rotate the mandrel at 1000 rpm for aligned fibres.
Store scaffolds on the aluminium foil under dry conditions.
Store in a sealed container at 4 °C with desiccant.
Set up the electrospinning rig as per Section 1, with PHBV spinning conditions.
Electrospin PHBV as above.
Without changing the aluminium foil, electrospin a second polymer on-top using the parameters and normal conditions for that polymer.
Anneal several layers of scaffolds by placing them together and heat annealing at 60 °C for 3 hours.
Anneal several sheets of PLGA suspended 2 cm above a pool of DCM in a sealed container at room temperature for 1 hour.
Produce an aseptic scaffold by electrospinning in a laminar flow hood inside a clean room.
Use sterile polymers of medical grade or sterilize polymers with DCM.
Dissolve the sterilized polymers.
Electrospin the dissolved polymers onto sterile foil wrapped around a sterilised mandrel.
Handle scaffolds aseptically after electrospinning.
Verify sterility by incubating scaffold samples in antibiotic-free growth media for an appropriate period.
Disinfect scaffolds with 70% ethanol for 15 minutes experimentally.
Sterilize scaffolds with peracetic acid (0.1% v/v in PBS) and incubate at room temperature for 3 hours.
Irradiate scaffolds with a dose of 3 kGy using a caesium source.
Cut scaffolds into rectangles measuring 5 mm x 20 mm.
Measure the thickness of each scaffold using a micrometer.
Place the measured scaffolds into a Bose Electroforce 3100 instrument.
Apply a force of 0-22 N up to a displacement of 6 mm in the instrument.
Plot the load vs. displacement as a stress/strain curve.
Calculate Young's modulus and elasticity from the plotted data.
Stain cells with vital fluorescent dyes to visualize cell attachment, migration, and proliferation on scaffolds.
Determine the presence of cells on scaffolds post culture by staining for cell nuclei with DAPI.
Assess ECM production by cells on scaffolds through staining for a range of ECM proteins including elastin.
Wash skin samples with PBS containing streptomycin, penicillin, and amphotericin B.
Incubate tissue samples in trypsin and glucose solution for 12-18 hours at 4°C.
Peel off the dermis and mince it finely.
Incubate minced dermis with collagenase solution at 37°C for 18 hours.
Centrifuge the resulting cell suspension at 400 g for 10 minutes to obtain a pellet of cells.
Culture and subculture fibroblasts in DMEM supplemented with FCS, streptomycin, penicillin, and amphotericin B.
Use fibroblasts from passages 4-9 for experiments.
Seed human dermal fibroblasts by adding trypsin/EDTA (5 ml, 5 mg/ml trypsin, 2 mg/ml EDTA in saline) to confluent cells in T75 flasks.
Incubate the cell suspension for 5 minutes at 37 °C.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 10 minutes at 150 g.
Resuspend the cells in 5 ml of DMEM supplemented with FCS (10% v/v), streptomycin (0.1 mg/ml), penicillin (100 IU/ml) and amphotericin B (0.5 μg/ml).
Count the cells using a haemocytometer.
Adjust the cell concentration for seeding at 50,000 cells per well.
Wash cells with 3 x 5 ml PBS if pre-labeling is required.
Add 10 mM CellTracker solution in serum-free medium (10 ml) to the cells and incubate for 45 minutes at 37 °C.
After incubation, wash the labeled cells with 3 x 5 ml PBS.
Seed the labeled cells onto scaffolds.
Image the surface of scaffolds using an Axon ImageExpress microscope at 570 nm λex - 620 nm λem for CellTracker red and 480 nm λex - 533 nm λem for CellTracker green.
Use a multiphoton confocal microscope to investigate cell penetration into scaffolds.
Fix post-culture samples in 1 ml 3.7% formaldehyde in PBS at 37 °C for 20 minutes.
Wash samples with 3 x 1 ml PBS.
Add 200 μL of elastin primary antibodies (5% v/v in PBS) to each sample and incubate at 37 °C for 30 minutes.
Wash samples with 3 x 1 ml PBS.
Incubate samples in a solution of secondary antibody (0.5% v/v goat anti-rabbit IgG (FC):FITC) in PBS containing DAPI (1 μg/ml) for 30 minutes.
Wash samples with 3 x 1 ml PBS.
Image DAPI and secondary antibody stained samples on an Axon ImageExpress fluorescent microscope, 365 nm λex - 460 nm λem for DAPI and 480 nm λex - 533 nm λem for the secondary antibody.
Assemble balloon and flow regulation apparatus and prepare system for sterile vessel suitable for cell culture once coated.
Autoclave the apparatus including the balloon at 122 °C, 220 mBar for 1 hour.
Unpack the apparatus in a laminar flow hood.
Inflate the balloon with phosphate buffered saline to the required surface area.
Connect the PBS to an electrical earth at a non-sterile point on the apparatus.
Electrospin the polymer onto the balloon using normal spinning conditions and a working distance of 10 cm.
Allow the scaffold to dry for 1 hour.
Place the balloon into a sterile vessel and transport it to a laminar flow hood suitable for cell culture.
Remove the balloon from the vessel and place it on a sterile surface (Petri dish).
Pipette a cell suspension (1 x 10^6 cells in 5 ml of DMEM) onto the coated balloon repeatedly every 20 seconds for 20 minutes.
Place the balloon into the culture vessel.
Add pre-warmed media appropriate to the cell type.
Connect the inflation apparatus to a syringe pump.
Inflate/deflate the balloon as required to give biaxial distension.
